html:
The United States occupied Nicaragua with Marines from 1912 to 1933, with a short break in 1925 and 1926. It was one of the longest of the American interventions in the Caribbean and Central America.

The Marines landed to protect a Conservative government that was friendly to American bankers, who controlled Nicaragua's customs and railway. A treaty of 1914 gave the United States the sole right to build a canal through Nicaragua, which it never used.

When civil war broke out in 1926 the Marines returned. The Liberal general Augusto César Sandino refused the peace deal and fought them in the northern mountains for six years. Before leaving in 1933, the Americans trained a National Guard and put Anastasio Somoza García at its head. The occupation was a model of the banana wars of the period.
sum: The United States occupied Nicaragua with Marines from 1912 to 1933, with a short break in 1925 and 1926. It was one of the longest of the American interventions in the Caribbean and Central America.
